items.headline: Reverse sweep! The Guardians dig out of an 0-2 hole and punch their ALCS ticket
items.body: What a turnaround. Down 0-2 and one loss from going home, the Guardians rattled off three straight wins over the upstart White Sox — capped by a 2-0 Game 5 shutout in Cleveland. José Ramírez supplied the only runs with a two-run homer, the pitching staff struck out 21 (!) Chicago hitters, and Cleveland completed the comeback. The White Sox's feel-good worst-to-wow run ends one step short; the Guardians move on to face the small-payroll Rays in the ALCS, starting Monday in Tampa.
items.say: You catch the Guardians? Down 0-2, looked dead, then won three in a row and shut out the White Sox to steal the series. Nothing in sports beats a comeback like that. You got a team still alive, or just here for the October chaos?

items.headline: Georgia survives the heavyweight bout — Dawgs edge Alabama 20-17 in Tuscaloosa
items.body: The biggest game on the board lived up to it. No. 2 Georgia walked into a deafening Bryant-Denny Stadium and out-slugged No. 6 Alabama 20-17 in a classic rock fight, winning it on a late field goal. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was surgical (18-of-22 for 249 yards and two touchdowns) and Georgia's run game ground out the clock. The Dawgs stay perfect at 6-0 and hand Alabama its first loss of the year.
items.say: Georgia-Alabama went down to the wire Saturday night — Georgia won it 20-17 on a late field goal in that crazy-loud stadium. Those two are always a slugfest. You follow any college ball on Saturdays, or just the pros?

items.headline: A two-year-old franchise is going to the Finals — the Valkyries sweep the champs
items.body: The best story in basketball got even better. The Golden State Valkyries — an expansion team that didn't exist two years ago — finished off a stunning sweep of the defending-champion Las Vegas Aces, closing it out 85-77 on the road to win the semifinal series 3-0. It's the franchise's first-ever WNBA Finals trip, in just its second season, behind coach Natalie Nakase. They'll meet Angel Reese's Atlanta Dream (who swept the Liberty) when the Finals tip off Oct. 17.
items.say: A WNBA team that's only two years old just swept the defending champs to reach the Finals — the Golden State Valkyries, this scrappy new franchise out in the Bay. Love an underdog story like that. You catch any of the W this year?

items.headline: Million-dollar Counter-Strike final today — MOUZ vs. Vitality in the Spodek
items.body: The Counter-Strike season reaches its climax today. After a week of playoffs in Katowice's roaring Spodek arena, it comes down to a best-of-five grand final between MOUZ and Team Vitality for the $1M prize pool (about $295K to the champs). There's a juicy storyline: MOUZ have reached a bunch of finals against Vitality and keep coming up just short — this is their shot at revenge on the sport's biggest stage.
items.say: That big Counter-Strike tournament in Poland has its million-dollar final today — two European powerhouses, best-of-five, winner takes a fortune. You ever watch any esports, or is it a total mystery to you?

items.headline: The 'mommy' that scared everyone wins the weekend — 'Other Mommy' tops the box office
items.body: Spooky season is paying off. 'Other Mommy,' the creepy Universal horror with Jessica Chastain in a dual role as a little girl's mom and the sinister thing imitating her, opened to about $27.5M to win the weekend box office. From 'Host' director Rob Savage, it rode a trailer that racked up tens of millions of views (and gave a lot of people nightmares) straight to No. 1. A nice October scare for the theater crowd.
items.say: That creepy 'Other Mommy' movie actually won the box office this weekend — the one with the fake mom in the trailer that freaked everybody out. Perfect October scare. You into the spooky stuff this time of year, or does it just stress you out?

items.headline: KATSEYE bring the arena tour home — North American run kicks off this week
items.body: If there's a teenager in your orbit, you've heard the name: KATSEYE, the globe-spanning pop group that blew up out of a reality competition, launch the North American leg of their first-ever arena tour (the 'WILDWORLD Tour') Tuesday in Miami, rolling through cities into late November. Their breakout hit 'Gabriela' is the kind of big, confident, impossible-not-to-move-to pop that turned them into one of the buzziest acts around.
items.say: This group KATSEYE is kicking off a big arena tour this week — they're kind of the pop group of the moment with the younger crowd. The songs are super catchy. You keep up with any of the new pop stuff, or is that firmly the kids' department now?

items.headline: A new 'Carrie' is here — Mike Flanagan reimagines Stephen King for the group-chat age
items.body: Horror fans, this one's a binge: Mike Flanagan's take on Stephen King's 'Carrie' just dropped all eight episodes on Prime Video. Newcomer Summer H. Howell plays the sheltered, bullied teen whose telekinetic powers awaken, with Samantha Sloyan as her terrifying mother. Flanagan ('The Haunting of Hill House') updates the classic for the social-media era — the infamous torment now goes viral — building to that prom night everyone knows is coming.
items.say: There's a new 'Carrie' series out from the horror guy who did Hill House — same Stephen King story, but set in the whole social-media, everything-goes-viral world now. Looks like a perfect October binge. You need a new show, or already got one going?

items.headline: Back to Camp Crystal Lake — the Jason Voorhees origin series lands Wednesday
items.body: Just in time for Friday-the-13th season: 'Crystal Lake,' the long-awaited prequel to the slasher franchise, premieres all eight episodes on Peacock this Wednesday (Oct. 15). From indie powerhouse A24, it rewinds to the small lakeside town before the legend, with Linda Cardellini as a young Pam Voorhees. Moody, bloody and dripping with camp-counselor dread — catnip for anyone who grew up on the movies.
items.say: They finally made that 'Crystal Lake' show — the Jason Voorhees origin story, out Wednesday. Right on time for spooky season. You ever into the old slasher movies, or more of a comfort-watch person?
